verdict.headline: Oil climbs to a four-week high as the Russia-Ukraine energy truce falters; stocks hold near record
verdict.label: Close: Brent $106.65 (+1.84%), highest since Sep 15; WTI $93.74 (+2.06%); S&P 500 7,807.24 (-0.06%), 11.69 pts under its record; Dow +0.38%; Nasdaq -0.44% on memory-chip selling; Micron -3.9%; gold ~$4,170 (-0.6%); BTC ~$81,365; bond market closed, 10Y ~5.24% Fri.
verdict.rationale_short: Brent settled up 1.8% at $106.65, its highest since September 15, after Zelensky said Russia had already violated the energy ceasefire President Trump announced and the Kremlin would say only that contacts were continuing. That reverses this morning's move: oil traded near $103 early on the truce and closed above Friday's $104.7 settlement, the level the morning report set for the market no longer trusting it. With no extra Russian supply in prospect, the weekend's Houthi strike on Riyadh and two tanker attacks were priced in. The S&P 500 slipped only 0.06% and nine of eleven sectors rose, so stocks absorbed higher oil; the Nasdaq's 0.44% loss came from memory makers after China's CXMT described a denser chip design. Wednesday's CPI, forecast at 3.6-3.7% headline, is the first print with a full month of Brent above $100, and Treasuries reopen Tuesday near 5.24%. If Brent falls back under $104.7 on a confirmed truce, this read no longer holds; a core CPI gain of 0.3% or more would likely take the ten-year through 5.331%.
verdict.lede_short: Oil rose to its highest since mid-September as Ukraine said Russia had already broken the energy truce President Trump announced, wiping out the morning's drop and closing above the level that marked the market losing faith in it. Stocks barely moved, with money rotating out of memory chips and into value. Wednesday's CPI is the first print with a full month of oil above $100; Brent back under $104.7 on a confirmed truce would change the picture.

supporting_data.label: Brent settled up $1.93 at $106.65 and WTI up 2.06% at $93.74 — oil closed more than $3 above its early low, so the truce rally lasted less than a session.

Zelensky said Russia violated the energy ceasefire, citing a strike on Naftogaz gas facilities in Kharkiv, while the Kremlin said only that contacts continue — with no confirmed deal, the market is pricing no extra Russian supply.
Forecasts put September CPI at 3.6-3.7% year on year, up from 3.4%, ahead of Wednesday's release — the first print with a full month of Brent above $100, landing as the Fed weighs a December hike.

China's CXMT said a new memory architecture can raise density 30-50%, with a server product due by the end of 2026 — Micron fell 3.9% and SanDisk 6.98% on the competitive threat, holding the S&P 500 under its record.
The Dow rose 0.38% to 51,850.55 while the Nasdaq fell 0.44% and the S&P 500 0.06% — money rotated from chips into value rather than leaving stocks, a day before bank earnings open the season.
Houthi missiles killed 12 at Riyadh's airport on Saturday and two more tankers were hit near Oman and Hormuz — once the truce came into doubt, the weekend's Gulf damage was priced in.

watchlist_mentions.note: Energy led nine of eleven rising S&P 500 sectors as Brent settled at $106.65, its highest since September 15, on the faltering Russia-Ukraine energy truce.
Closed down 1.29% at $226.32, about 5% under its $239.24 October 6 record, as memory makers led chips lower; ASML Wednesday and TSMC Thursday are the next tests.
Fell 3.9%, the largest drag on the Nasdaq, after CXMT said a new architecture raises memory density 30-50%; still up about 245% this year.
Reports Tuesday with Goldman Sachs, Citigroup and Wells Fargo as Treasuries reopen near 5.24% with Brent about $2 higher than Friday.
Down 2.7% over 24 hours to about $81,365 on Crypto.com, 1.3% above Thursday's $80,320 low; ether fell 4.3%.

trade_setups.thesis: Brent closed above the $104.7 line the morning report set for the market no longer trusting the energy truce, reaching its highest since September 15 as Kyiv alleged violations and Moscow declined to confirm the deal.
trade_setups.invalidation: A confirmed truce and a halt to grid and refinery strikes would put Brent back under $104.7; further strikes or a Houthi hit that stops Saudi loadings would take it toward the September highs.
trade_setups.horizon: October 13-16, with the IEA board meeting October 14-15

trade_setups.thesis: Treasuries reopen Tuesday near 5.24%, 9 basis points under the 5.331% high, with Brent about $2 higher than when bonds last traded and CPI due Wednesday.
trade_setups.entry: Ten-year ~5.24%; high 5.331%; core CPI forecast +0.2% m/m; December hike odds above 75% on CME FedWatch as of October 2.
trade_setups.invalidation: A core monthly gain of 0.3% or more would likely take the ten-year through 5.331%; 0.2% or less would ease pressure on stocks near their record.

trade_setups.thesis: Memory makers led chips lower on CXMT's denser design; Nvidia sits about 5% under its record and the S&P 500 is held under its own by the sector.
trade_setups.entry: S&P 500 7,807.24; record 7,818.93 above, 7,666.45 below; Nvidia $226.32 vs $239.24 record.
trade_setups.invalidation: Steady TSMC guidance would confine the selling to memory; an S&P 500 close under 7,666.45 would show it spreading.
